name: Built-up share (year)
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: How much of the hexagon is built up in that year.
how: Pixels classified "Built area" / all valid pixels in the hexagon (clouds and no-data excluded).

name: Land-use mix (year)
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: How mixed the land cover is: 0 = one cover type only, 1 = all eight types in equal parts.
how: Shannon entropy of the 8 land-cover class shares, divided by ln 8.

name: Built-up share, start
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Built-up share at the start of the study period.
how: Mean of the first two years (config lulc.early).

name: Built-up share, latest
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Built-up share now.
how: Mean of the last two years (config lulc.late).

name: Built-up growth
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: How much the built-up share rose over the study period.
how: bu_late - bu_early, in percentage points.

name: Built-up trend
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Typical yearly rise of the built-up share, robust to single odd years.
how: Theil-Sen slope (median of all pairwise yearly slopes) of the yearly built-up share.

name: Land-use mix change
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Negative = the area is becoming more uniform (e.g. farmland turning into continuous city).
how: mix_late - mix_early (same two-year means as built-up).

name: Open land left
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Share of the hexagon that is neither built up nor water in the latest year - room left to build.
how: 1 - built share - water share (latest year).

name: Neighbour growth, ring k
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Average built-up growth of the hexagons exactly k steps away (ring 1 = the 6 touching hexes; at H3 level 8 rings 1-4 lie on average about 0.9 / 1.7 / 2.5 / 3.3 km away).
how: Mean of built_change_pp over the ring-k hexagons.

name: Neighbourhood growth pull
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: How strongly the surroundings (rings 1-4, closest counting most) are building up.
how: Weighted mean of ring 1..4 growth with weights 1, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4.

name: Growth hotspot score
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Is this hexagon part of a statistically unusual cluster of fast (positive) or slow (negative) growth?
how: Getis-Ord Gi* of built_change_pp over the hexagon and its rings 1-2 (same statistic as Pro's Hot Spot Analysis; no FDR correction).

name: Growth hotspot class
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: 3 / 2 / 1 = growth hot spot at 99 / 95 / 90 % confidence, negative = cold spot, 0 = not significant.
how: |z| >= 2.576 / 1.960 / 1.645, as Pro's Gi_Bin field.

name: Newly built-up area
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Land that became built up between the start and the latest years (built in both latest years, in neither start year).
how: 30 m cells, patches under 2 cells dropped as noise.

name: Type of new built-up
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Infill fills gaps inside existing built-up; edge extends it outward; leapfrog is detached new development (sprawl).
how: Landscape Expansion Index (Liu et al. 2010): share of the one-cell ring around each new patch that was already built: >50 % infill, >0 edge, 0 leapfrog.

name: Growth type
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: One-word summary of what is happening in the hexagon.
how: If new built-up >= grow_pp % of the hex: its dominant type (Infill / Edge / Leapfrog growth). Otherwise: "Growth frontier" when growth pull >= frontier_pp and open land >= open_min; else "Built-up, stable" (built share >= built_core) or "Open land, stable".

name: Forecast built-up growth
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual) + OSM roads/transit
short: Expected rise of the built-up share over the next few years if recent patterns continue.
how: Gradient-boosted model trained on past hex transitions: own built-up share and recent change, land-use mix, open-land types, rings 1-4 built-up and change, distances to malls, centre, roads, rail. No population data is used.

name: Forecast range
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Likely low and high end of the forecast (10th and 90th percentile models).
how: Quantile gradient-boosting models, same inputs.

name: Population
source: Esri Business Analyst (offline), enriched in ArcGIS Pro
short: Residents in the hexagon (Business Analyst current year).
how: TOTPOP_CY.

name: Purchasing power
source: Esri Business Analyst (offline), enriched in ArcGIS Pro
short: Total purchasing power of residents. Treat with caution: modelled values can be unrealistic in special areas such as cantonments.
how: PP_CY.

name: Projected population growth
source: Esri Business Analyst (offline), enriched in ArcGIS Pro
short: Shown for information only; NOT used in any score (the projections are close to linear).

name: Distance to nearest mall
source: city.yaml mall list
short: Straight-line distance to the nearest listed mall.
how: Hex centroid to mall point.

name: Malls within 15 minutes
source: Pro Network Analyst (15-min service areas)
short: How many listed malls can reach this hexagon within a 15-minute drive.
how: Hex centroid inside each mall's 15-min polygon.

name: Mall gap
source: mall list + 15-min areas
short: Distance to the nearest mall, capped at 8 km; cut to 30 % if the hexagon is already inside some mall's 15-minute area.
how: min(dist, 8) / 8 x (0.3 if covered).

name: Transit access
source: OpenStreetMap
short: Bus stops plus rail/metro stations within 1 km (a station counts 5).
how: Sum of stop weights within 1 km of the hex centroid.

name: Excluded area
source: OpenStreetMap military/cantonment polygons + your exclude.geojson
short: Hexagons ruled out for a new mall (military land, cantonment, or areas you excluded).
how: >= min_overlap of the hex area inside an exclusion polygon, or listed in exclude.hex_ids.

name: Opportunity score
source: all of the above
short: Where a new mall would find people, growth and few competitors. Only for hexagons that are already somewhat urban, populated and not excluded.
how: Weighted mean of percentiles among eligible hexagons: people, spending, built-up growth (observed), forecast growth, neighbourhood pull, mall gap, transit. Weights are the sliders in the app.

name: People
source: Esri Business Analyst (offline), enriched in ArcGIS Pro
short: Population of the hexagon.
how: Percentile of pop.

name: Spending power
source: Esri Business Analyst (offline), enriched in ArcGIS Pro
short: Purchasing power (low default weight - see caveat).
how: Percentile of spend.

name: Recent built-up growth
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Observed growth over the study period.
how: Percentile of built_change_pp.

name: Forecast growth
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Expected growth over the forecast horizon.
how: Percentile of fc_gain_pp.

name: Neighbourhood pull
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Growth in the surrounding rings.
how: Percentile of growth_pull_pp.

name: Mall gap
source: mall list
short: Distance from existing malls.
how: Percentile of gap.

name: Transit
source: OpenStreetMap
short: Public-transport access.
how: Percentile of transit.

name: People within 15 min
source: Esri Business Analyst (offline), enriched in ArcGIS Pro + 15-min service area
short: Residents of the hexagons inside the mall's 15-minute drive area.
how: Sum of hex pop (hex centroid inside the polygon).

name: Purchasing power per person
source: Esri Business Analyst (offline), enriched in ArcGIS Pro
short: Average purchasing power of those residents.
how: Sum of spend / sum of pop.

name: Shared catchment
source: 15-min service areas
short: Share of the mall's 15-minute population that another listed mall can also reach in 15 minutes.
how: Population of hexes also inside another mall's polygon / pop.

name: Nearest other mall
source: mall list
short: Straight-line distance to the closest other listed mall.

name: Brand outlets per 100k people
source: Business Analyst POIs (your JSON export)
short: Stand-alone outlets of the malls' tenant brands in the 15-minute area, per 100,000 residents.
how: POIs matched to tenant brands by name, inside the polygon / (pop / 100,000).

name: Built-up share now (catchment)
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: How built up the 15-minute area is.
how: Mean of bu_late over its hexagons.

name: Built-up growth (catchment)
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Rise of the built-up share in the 15-minute area over the study period.
how: Mean of hex built_change_pp.

name: Forecast growth (catchment)
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Expected further rise over the forecast horizon.
how: Mean of hex fc_gain_pp.

name: Growth hotspot share
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Share of the 15-minute area's hexagons that are growth hot spots (95 % confidence or more).
how: hotspot_bin >= 2.

name: Tenant mix score (absolute)
source: mall tenant list (website)
short: Quality of the mall's own tenant mix on a fixed scale (not compared with other malls).
how: 100 x (0.30 category variety + 0.25 rating quality + 0.25 premium share + 0.20 anchor coverage). Variety = entropy of category-group shares / ln(9 groups); premium share scores 100 at 30 % premium brands; anchors = share of 6 anchor types present (department store, supermarket, electronics, entertainment, food court, luxury); rating quality = Bayesian-shrunk star rating, used only if at least 30 % of every listed mall's stores have ratings, otherwise its weight is shared out among the other three.

name: A · Tenant mix
source: tenant lists (all malls)
short: Variety, premium share and anchors of the tenant list, relative to the other malls.
how: A_abs scaled across malls. Only when every mall has a tenant list.

name: B · Competitive headroom
source: 15-min service areas
short: Higher = less competition from other malls for the same shoppers.
how: 100 x (1 - (0.5 shared catchment + 0.3 other malls per hex + 0.2 closeness of nearest mall)), each scaled across malls.

name: C · Reachability
source: Esri Business Analyst (offline), enriched in ArcGIS Pro + OSM
short: How many people and how much public transport the 15-minute area holds.
how: 100 x (0.7 population + 0.3 transit), scaled across malls.

name: D · Spending power
source: Esri Business Analyst (offline), enriched in ArcGIS Pro
short: Purchasing power and density of the catchment (low default weight).
how: 100 x (0.5 total purchasing power + 0.25 per person + 0.25 population density), scaled across malls.

name: E · Growth momentum
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: How fast the catchment is building up, now and in the forecast. No population projections.
how: 100 x (0.5 observed built-up growth + 0.5 forecast growth), scaled across malls.

name: G · Brand ecosystem
source: Business Analyst POIs
short: Outlets of the tenant brands per 100k people around the mall (market depth).
how: brand_per_100k scaled across malls.

name: H · Brand differentiation
source: tenant lists (all malls)
short: Share of the mall's brands that its competitors (malls with overlapping 15-min areas) do not have.
how: 1 - shared-brand share, scaled across malls. Only when every mall has a tenant list.

name: Composite score
source: indices above
short: Weighted average of the indices (weights = sliders).
how: Sum of weight x index; weights re-normalised to 100 % over the indices available.

name: Rank range
source: composite
short: How stable the rank is: the rank in the best 10 % and worst 10 % of 500 random re-weightings around the chosen weights.
how: Dirichlet(25 x weights) draws.

name: Built-up reach by direction
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: How far, in each of 8 compass directions, the continuous built-up area stretches from the focus point (subject mall or city centre) before it drops below 50 %.
how: Built-up share of 2 km distance bands within each 45-degree sector, crossing point of 50 % interpolated; "beyond" = still above 50 % at the edge of the study area.

name: Land-use mix, start / latest
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Land-use mix averaged over the start / latest two years.
how: Mean of mix_<year>.

name: Land-cover class shares (latest year)
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: What the hexagon is made of in the latest year besides built-up.
how: Class pixels / valid pixels.

name: Neighbour built-up share, ring k
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: How built up the ring-k neighbours are now.
how: Mean of bu_late over the ring-k hexagons.

name: Forecast built-up share
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Built-up share expected at the end of the forecast horizon.
how: Latest (two-year mean) built-up share + fc_gain_pp.

name: Newly built-up area
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Area that became built up (sum of infill, edge and leapfrog).
how: infill_km2 + edge_km2 + leapfrog_km2.

name: Hexagon area
source: H3 grid
short: Area of the hexagon.
how: Polygon area in the metric CRS.

name: Land-cover data coverage
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Lowest share of valid (not cloud / no-data) pixels over the years; below 0.5 a year is left blank, below 0.7 the hexagon is not scored.
how: Valid pixels / all pixels, minimum over years.

name: Eligible for the opportunity score
source: rules
short: Built-up >= 20 %, population >= 1,500, data coverage >= 0.7 and not excluded (defaults; see city.yaml eligibility).
how: All rules true.

name: Why excluded
source: OSM / your files
short: Military land (OSM), cantonment (OSM), your exclude.geojson or your hex id list.
how: First rule that matched.

name: Nearest mall
source: city.yaml
short: Name of the nearest listed mall.

name: Purchasing power (catchment)
source: Esri Business Analyst (offline), enriched in ArcGIS Pro
short: Total purchasing power of the residents of the 15-minute area.
how: Sum of hex spend.

name: Population density
source: Esri Business Analyst (offline), enriched in ArcGIS Pro
short: Residents per km2 of the 15-minute area.
how: pop / (hexagons x hexagon area).

name: Transit access (catchment)
source: OpenStreetMap
short: Average transit access of the hexagons in the 15-minute area.
how: Mean of hex transit.

name: Other malls per hexagon
source: 15-min service areas
short: On average, how many other listed malls also reach each hexagon of the 15-minute area.
how: Mean over hexagons of (malls reaching it - 1).

name: Brand outlets in catchment
source: Business Analyst POIs
short: Stand-alone outlets of the tenant brands inside the 15-minute area.
how: POIs inside the polygon.

name: Neighbourhood growth pull (catchment)
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Average neighbourhood growth pull of the hexagons in the 15-minute area.
how: Mean of hex growth_pull_pp.

name: Excluded share of catchment
source: exclusions
short: Share of the 15-minute area's hexagons that are excluded areas (military land, cantonment ...).
how: Mean of hex excluded.

key: gt_infill / gt_edge / gt_leapfrog / gt_growth / gt_built_up / gt_open
name: Growth-type mix of the catchment
source: Esri Sentinel-2 10 m Land Use/Land Cover (annual)
short: Share of the 15-minute area's hexagons by growth type (growth = growth frontier, built_up = built-up stable, open = open land stable).
how: Counts of growth_type / hexagons.

name: Hexagons in catchment
source: 15-min service area
short: Number of hexagons whose centre lies in the 15-minute area.

name: Rank details
source: composite
short: Rank with the default weights; median rank over 500 random re-weightings; share of those re-weightings in which the mall is in the top 3.
how: Dirichlet(25 x weights) draws.

name: Brand overlap with competitors
source: tenant lists
short: Share of the mall's brands its competitors also have (feeds H), and how many competitors (malls whose 15-min area overlaps > 5 % of its own).
